subject: Themberchaud
fact: Themberchaud is a young red dragon, pampered and polished, serving as a glorified lighter for the Duergar forges in Gracklstugh. He believes himself to be a powerful ruler but is deeply manipulated, unaware of his true role. His scales are meticulously kept shiny, his claws painted, and his demeanor childish and vain. He has a second chin and speaks with inflated authority, yet lacks strategic understanding. He thinks he is in charge of his realm, but is merely a tool.
source_quote: Climb aboard, unless you wish to question the will of your wormsmith.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a half-orc cleric of Bahamut, experienced in escapes and prison breaks, deeply aware of the manipulation of powerful beings. He is pragmatic, spiritually appalled by Themberchaud’s degradation, and attempts to navigate the dragon’s ego with flattery and subtle truth. He volunteers to take risks, including betting on his own survival.
source_quote: You’re not one of the peons who understands the little things. But we are as little as you get, and we can find the little things that are big for us.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a cautious, observant member of the party who fears collateral damage from dragon-led chaos. He is relieved when the group avoids destructive decisions and relies on his own magical ability (Misty Step) to survive falls. He notices the dragon’s lack of control and the vulnerability of his companions.
source_quote: I do not want to have a dragon destroy a city while I am on its back.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a seasoned observer of powerful, egotistical figures, recognizing Themberchaud’s need for face-saving gestures. He intervenes with a strategic lie to redirect the dragon’s attention toward the docks, using the dragon’s own sense of superiority to manipulate him into action.
source_quote: There was an attack on the docks, so there might be new intelligence. Your agents didn’t miss it; they just haven’t been there recently.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is skeptical and reluctant to share information, preferring secrecy. He mutters dismissively about revealing everything, indicating a distrustful and guarded nature, but does not actively oppose the group’s decisions.
source_quote: We should just tell him everything. Nah.

subject: Jimjar
fact: Jimjar is a ghoul with a morbid sense of humor, quick to make bets about survival in dangerous situations. He openly questions Grygum’s likelihood of surviving peril, treating life-and-death moments as entertainment.
source_quote: Anyone want to make a bet that Grygum is going to survive?

subject: Duergar
fact: The Duergar are a subterranean dwarven faction who exploit Themberchaud as a living tool — a glorified lighter — for their forges, despite his immense power. They manipulate him through pampering and false authority, suppressing his true nature to maintain control. Their use of a red dragon instead of magic reveals a preference for psychological domination over efficiency.
source_quote: I wonder why the Duergar chose a Red Dragon? Surely magic would be cheaper and less dangerous.

subject: Themberchaud
fact: Themberchaud is a young red dragon, physically large but emotionally stunted and physically softened by pampering. He lacks the predatory grace, sharp claws, or battle-worn scales of a true dragon. His flight is clumsy, his landing ungainly, and his behavior childish. He is not a threat by nature, but his manipulation makes him unpredictable. He is a creature of power rendered harmless by his role.
source_quote: I need to show you my realm.

subject: Gracklstugh
fact: Gracklstugh is a Duergar stronghold in the Underdark, dominated by forges, thick smoke, and oppressive darkness. It is the site of Themberchaud’s enslavement and the center of his delusions of grandeur. The city’s atmosphere is one of industrial decay and psychological control, where even dragons are reduced to tools.
source_quote: the forges of the Duergar

subject: Dark Lake District
fact: The Dark Lake District is a lawless, dangerous area near the docks of Gracklstugh, known for petty crime, traitors, and hidden intelligence. It is the target of the party’s investigation, but Themberchaud dismisses it as beneath his station, revealing his disconnect from ground-level reality.
source_quote: loiter among the common rabble and petty traitors of the Dark Lake

subject: dragon flight from Gracklstugh
fact: The party mounts Themberchaud and takes flight through the smoky caverns of Gracklstugh. The dragon declares himself their ruler and attempts to show them his 'realm,' but his flight is ungraceful and unstable. During a sudden turn, multiple party members fall, forcing magical interventions. The event exposes Themberchaud’s lack of control and the party’s vulnerability.
source_quote: Themberchaud takes off with a powerful beat of his wings, proudly declaring, 'I need to show you my realm'.

subject: falling incident during flight
fact: During a sharp maneuver by Themberchaud, several party members — including Grygum and Thorin — fall from his back. Daz uses Misty Step to save himself. Zalthir grows wings and rescues Thorin. The event highlights the danger of trusting a manipulated, unskilled dragon and the improvisational survival skills of the party.
source_quote: And then I am falling. Not for long, that’s what Misty Step is for.

subject: Themberchaud’s true role
fact: The party is aware that Themberchaud is not a sovereign but a glorified lighter for the Duergar, yet they must conceal this knowledge to survive. His delusions of power and the group’s need to manipulate him create a fragile, high-stakes tension. Uncovering his true function could destabilize the Duergar’s control — or trigger his wrath.
source_quote: My Bahamut-trained sensibilities are appalled at how they treat Themberchaud.

subject: attack on the docks
fact: An unconfirmed attack on the docks of the Dark Lake District is the proposed lead for investigation. Zalthir suggests it as a plausible reason to go there, but its actual existence is uncertain — possibly fabricated to appease Themberchaud’s ego. The truth of the attack remains unresolved and critical to the mission.
source_quote: There was an attack on the docks, so there might be new intelligence.

subject: Themberchaud’s painted claws
fact: Themberchaud’s claws are painted, a deliberate cosmetic choice that contradicts their intended function as weapons of destruction. They show no signs of battle, wear, or use — instead appearing decorative, like a toy’s. This detail symbolizes his complete domestication and the Duergar’s psychological control.
source_quote: his claws are painted. They have none of the telltale signs of rending and destruction that they should have.

subject: Themberchaud’s polished scales
fact: Themberchaud’s scales are meticulously polished to a high shine, an unnatural and obsessive grooming that renders him visually incongruous with a true dragon. This detail reflects his role as a status symbol rather than a warrior — a pet maintained for appearance, not power.
source_quote: his scales are shiny. Someone has been carefully keeping them polished.

subject: session date
fact: The events occur during the current expedition into Gracklstugh, following the party’s escape from previous Duergar and Drow prisons. The timeline is continuous, with no indication of elapsed time between prior events and this dragon-assisted journey.
source_quote: I have a gift for this. I suppose.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a giant who believes in bold, chaotic action, often disregarding consequences. He recently shouted about a 'flyby to the docks' and invoked an old saying: 'To save the village, you must smash the village.' He has shown a pattern of ignoring advice and rolling the dice on dangerous decisions.
source_quote: Alright, one more flyby and to the docks!

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a thoughtful, weary leader who weighs moral consequences and seeks to minimize bloodshed. He recognizes the group's false identity as the Ember Vanguard and uses it strategically. He is deeply aware of the secrets they carry and finds comfort in knowing they prevented mass destruction in Gracklstugh.
source_quote: The secrets we carried — of the Deep King’s plots, the corrupted dragon egg, and the lurking demonic plots — could have provoked mass death and destruction. And we took those secrets with us.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a perceptive member of the group whose presence triggers panic among the Duergar, leading them to believe the group is the Ember Vanguard. He is not impressed by Themberchaud’s theatrics and notes the Duergar’s disdain for him.
source_quote: The Duergar are rolling their eyes. They don’t take him as seriously as he takes himself.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a cleric who acts with ritual precision and symbolic intent. He deputizes the Duergar guard with a caltrop as a token of their mission, and later suggests scuttling the boat — showing a blend of faith and pragmatism.
source_quote: This is a symbol of our mission. Guard it and keep it secret.

subject: Themberchaud
fact: Themberchaud is a dragon who believes himself to be the Wyrmsmith, a divine forger of flame. He loudly proclaims his identity, breathes fire at forges, and insists on dramatic flybys — all while being completely oblivious to the group’s strategic concerns.
source_quote: I am Themberchaud the Wyrmsmith, bringer of flame!

subject: Sarith
fact: Sarith is driven by strange compulsions, previously drawn to Myconid dancing in the Whorlstone Caverns and now compelled to reach the Neverlight Grove. He is intuitive, not logical, and insists on leaving the boat despite the risk.
source_quote: The path to the Neverlight Grove goes past the Lost Tomb of Khaem. But we must leave the boat here.

subject: Rump-a-dump
fact: Rump-a-dump is a childlike member of the group who believes in the inviolability of sacred circles and refuses to acknowledge danger. He speaks with naive certainty about his sovereign’s protection.
source_quote: Zalthir, the circle cannot be corrupted. Our sovereign would never let that happen.

subject: Jimjar
fact: Jimjar is a reckless gambler who makes absurd bets with cryptic, prophetic phrasing. He recently wagered an empty shell gem that a 'circle of joy' will become a 'circle of unwilling vows,' unsettling the group.
source_quote: I'll bet you an empty shell gem that this circle of joy will reveal itself to be a circle of unwilling vows before you leave it.

subject: Gartokkar
fact: Gartokkar is a warning voice who has alerted the group that everyone in Gracklstugh is on edge and actively searching for the Ember Vanguard. His reports shape the group’s perception of their false identity.
source_quote: The Stone Guard is looking for the Ember Vanguard, the powerful mercenary group, and the Grey Ghosts are looking for the Ember Vanguard, and the Deep King is worried.

subject: Ember Vanguard
fact: The Ember Vanguard is a feared, legendary mercenary group believed to be responsible for chaos and destruction in the Underdark. The party is mistaken for them, triggering panic among Duergar and Drow. Their reputation precedes them, even though they are impostors.
source_quote: They think we are the Ember Vanguard.

subject: Duergar
fact: The Duergar of Gracklstugh are deeply suspicious, militarized, and terrified of the Ember Vanguard. They are unafraid of Themberchaud but react with immediate panic upon seeing Daz, confirming their belief that the group is the legendary threat.
source_quote: They weren’t afraid of Themberchaud but when they saw Daz, they suddenly freaked out.

subject: Deep King
fact: The Deep King is a powerful, shadowy ruler whose plots and corrupted dragon egg the party carries as secrets. His authority is invoked by the Stone Guard, and his fear of the Ember Vanguard is a key driver of the city’s paranoia.
source_quote: Halt in the name of the Deep King!

subject: Grey Ghosts
fact: The Grey Ghosts are a mysterious group actively hunting the Ember Vanguard, contributing to the paranoia in Gracklstugh. Their presence is mentioned as part of the city-wide search, though their nature and motives remain obscure.
source_quote: The Grey Ghosts are looking for the Ember Vanguard.

subject: Gracklstugh
fact: Gracklstugh is a Dwarven city in the Underdark, filled with paranoia, militarized guards, and hidden secrets. It is the site of the party’s false identity as the Ember Vanguard and the place from which they escaped with dangerous knowledge.
source_quote: The people of Gracklstugh owe us, even if they are unaware of it.

subject: Neverlight Grove
fact: The Neverlight Grove is a mysterious, dangerous location in the Underdark rumored to be corrupted by demonic influence. It draws Sarith and others through compulsion, despite its lethal reputation.
source_quote: There is a very dangerous and mighty demon there, and that we might not want to go there at all.

subject: Lost Tomb of Khaem
fact: The Lost Tomb of Khaem is a hidden ruin on the path to the Neverlight Grove, believed to contain a powerful weapon. The group plans to visit it before proceeding, hoping to arm themselves against the dangers ahead.
source_quote: Perhaps we could first go to the Lost Tomb of Khaem, secure whatever weapon it has, and then go?

subject: Whorlstone Caverns
fact: The Whorlstone Caverns are a location previously visited by the party, where Sarith was mysteriously drawn to dancing Myconids. This experience now influences his compulsion toward the Neverlight Grove.
source_quote: The strange compulsion that drew him to the dancing Myconids in the Whorlstone Caverns draws him to the grove.

subject: caltrop
fact: A caltrop is used by Grygum as a symbolic token of the group’s mission. He gives it to the Duergar guard to bind him to secrecy, transforming a mundane object into a sacred relic of deception.
source_quote: This is a symbol of our mission. Guard it and keep it secret.

subject: empty shell gem
fact: An empty shell gem is the wagered item in Jimjar’s bizarre bet about the Neverlight Grove. It represents his tendency toward cryptic gambling and foreshadows a future, possibly cursed, ritual.
source_quote: I'll bet you an empty shell gem that this circle of joy will reveal itself to be a circle of unwilling vows before you leave it.

subject: escape from Gracklstugh
fact: The party escaped Gracklstugh by exploiting their mistaken identity as the Ember Vanguard, causing panic among the Duergar and securing time to flee. They left behind no direct evidence but carried dangerous secrets that could have triggered mass destruction.
source_quote: We came to find equipment, and we did that. And as Daz said, we betrayed many people.

subject: departure from the boat
fact: The party abandoned their boat on the 7th day of the 2nd tenday, knowing it would leave a trail for pursuers. They debated scuttling it but chose to leave it intact, increasing risk but preserving potential future utility.
source_quote: Leaving the boat is like leaving a sign. But we might need it later.

subject: circle of unwilling vows
fact: Jimjar’s bet implies a hidden, possibly demonic ritual awaiting the party in the Neverlight Grove — one that will force them into binding, unwilling oaths. The nature of this thread is cryptic, but its implications are ominous.
source_quote: I'll bet you an empty shell gem that this circle of joy will reveal itself to be a circle of unwilling vows before you leave it.

subject: corrupted dragon egg
fact: The party carries a secret: a corrupted dragon egg, likely tied to the Deep King’s plots. Its existence could trigger catastrophic events if revealed, and its fate remains unresolved as they flee deeper into the Underdark.
source_quote: The secrets we carried — of the Deep King’s plots, the corrupted dragon egg, and the lurking demonic plots — could have provoked mass death and destruction.

subject: 4th-6th day of the 2nd tenday of Myrtul 1493
fact: The first three days of travel were uneventful, marked by rowing, darkness, and strange sounds. On the third day, bloodsucking giant mosquitoes attacked but were swiftly killed.
source_quote: The third day brings excitement when some bloodsucking giant mosquitoes fall from the roof.

subject: 7th day of the 2nd tenday of Myrtul 1493
fact: On the 7th day, the party abandoned their boat and entered the Underdark on foot, beginning their journey toward the Lost Tomb of Khaem and the Neverlight Grove. The date marks the transition from maritime to terrestrial travel.
source_quote: On the fourth day, Sarith announces that we must get out on a beach and head deeper into the Underdark on foot.

subject: naval demand for mending
fact: Navies were in high demand for spellcasters who could cast mending, but spellcasters tended to avoid learning the spell because in naval combat, the first person killed was the mender — until they were dead, the ship could not be sunk.
source_quote: Well, spell casters who could cast mending were in high demand by the navies. And so spellcasters tended to avoid learning that spell. See, in naval combat, the first person you kill is the mender. Because until you kill him, you can’t sink the ship. So finding a spell caster who can cast it is rare.
